PROTOTYPE TEST DATA — NOT AN OFFICIAL CMPDI/CIL DOCUMENT Page 2 TESTING PURPOSE This sample is intentionally structured like a technical annual geological exploration report so that the prototype can be tested against realistic document-processing tasks. It contains headings, narrative text, tables, numerical values, units, dates, repeated entities, historical comparisons, exploration activities and deliberate validation cases. Recommended prototype functions to test: 1. OCR and text extraction 2. Table extraction 3. Geological field extraction 4. Numerical and unit normalization 5. Cross-table validation 6. Document search and semantic retrieval 7. Topic identification and word cloud generation 8. AI question answering with source/page citations 9. Automated annual-report generation 10. Detection of intentionally inserted inconsistencies. 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY During the 2024–25 reporting period, the Exploration Division conducted geological exploration activities across selected coal-bearing blocks in the Central Sector. The programme covered reconnaissance, regional exploration, detailed exploration, drilling, geological mapping, core logging, sampling and laboratory analysis. The illustrative programme recorded 18,460 metres of drilling against a planned 17,800 metres. The exploration programme focused on improving geological confidence, evaluating coal seam continuity, estimating resources and supporting future mine planning. The test dataset includes information from four illustrative exploration blocks: Karanpur East, Shakti North, Nandini Extension and Surya South. The prototype should be able to identify the difference between planned and achieved drilling, extract resource estimates, identify the highest drilling achievement, compare coal quality parameters, and retrieve evidence for each answer. 2. MAJOR FINDINGS The illustrative exploration programme indicates increased drilling activity compared with the previous two reporting periods. The largest individual drilling contribution in the current test dataset is associated with Surya South. Resource estimates show variation in the relative proportions of measured, indicated and inferred categories. Coal quality parameters also vary among blocks. The prototype should not merely summarize this section. It should independently calculate findings from the underlying tables and identify whether the narrative agrees with the structured data. 12. CHALLENGES OBSERVED DURING EXPLORATION Illustrative operational challenges included delays in access to selected drill locations, weather-related interruptions, variation in core recovery, differences in historical document formats and delays in receiving laboratory results. These statements are synthetic test content and are intended to test topic extraction and classification. 13. RECOMMENDATIONS Future exploration programmes may prioritize areas with insufficient geological confidence, improve digital capture of borehole information, standardize data dictionaries, increase structured storage of laboratory results and establish consistent document templates across reporting cycles. For the AI prototype, standardized metadata and controlled vocabularies should be maintained alongside the original documents. 14. SIH Problem Statement 26023 | Prototype & Real-Data Testing Document 1. Executive Summary Problem Statement 26023 addresses the highly manual process of compiling information from scanned PDFs, digital documents, spreadsheets, images and historical archives for geological, mining, production and other reporting requirements. The proposed prototype is an AI-assisted document intelligence and reporting platform that converts heterogeneous source material into searchable, validated and traceable information and then supports automated report generation, topic/word-cloud analysis and natural-language question answering. The prototype is intended to be a working model rather than a presentation-only mock-up. Testing will use real or authorized operational data where permitted, together with sanitized/de-identified data when confidentiality prevents direct use. Every extracted value should retain a link to its source document, page, table or cell so that users can verify the result. 2. Problem Statement Understanding Area Prototype Interpretation Input challenge Information exists across scanned PDFs, native PDFs, Word files, Excel spreadsheets, images and historical archives. Current difficulty Manual reading, extraction, comparison and report preparation creates delays and increases the chance of transcription or interpretation errors. Core requirement Digitize/extract information, validate it, preserve provenance, and make it available for reporting and AI-assisted queries. Primary modules Automated Report Generation; Word Cloud & Topic Identification; AI Query & Response. Expected value Faster reporting, improved consistency and traceability, easier retrieval of historical information, and reduced repetitive work. 3. Prototype Goals • Build an end-to-end working prototype that accepts multiple document/data formats. • Extract text, tables, metadata and relevant numerical values from source material. • Process scanned documents through OCR and normalize extracted content into a common representation. • Validate important geological, mining and production figures using configurable rules and cross-document checks. • Store document versions, extracted records and source references for traceability. • Generate structured reports from selected data and source documents. • Identify important topics, terms and trends from a collection of reports. • Allow users to ask natural-language questions and receive answers grounded in the uploaded/authorized data. • Measure extraction accuracy, response quality, automation rate and processing time using a controlled test dataset. • Design the architecture so that it can later be integrated with CIL/CMPDI workflows. 4. Prototype Scope 4.1 In Scope • PDF ingestion: native and scanned PDFs. • Word document ingestion. • Excel/CSV ingestion for structured figures. • Image ingestion where documents/tables are provided as images. • OCR for scanned pages. • Document classification and metadata extraction. • Text/table extraction and normalization. • Search and retrieval across authorized documents.

SIH Problem Statement 26023 | Prototype & Real-Data Testing Document • Rule-based validation of extracted figures and fields. • Source/page/table/cell-level provenance wherever technically available. • Automated report generation in a structured template. • Word-cloud generation and topic identification. • AI-assisted question answering using retrieved source evidence. • Dashboard for processing status, validation results, reports and query history. • Evaluation framework with manually verified ground truth. 4.2 Out of Scope for Initial Prototype • Replacing official CIL/CMPDI approval or sign-off processes. • Autonomous publication of official reports without human review. • Uncontrolled ingestion of confidential information. • Making operational decisions without authorized human validation. • Training a foundation model from scratch. • Claiming 100% extraction accuracy before benchmark testing. 5. Proposed System Architecture Recommended architecture: Python is used for the AI/document-processing layer, while JavaScript/TypeScript is used for the web application and user experience. An API layer connects the frontend to the Python processing services. Layer Technology Direction Responsibility Prototype Output Frontend Next.js / React + Tailwind CSS Upload, search, dashboards, validation review, reports and chat UI Web application Backend/API Node.js/Express or Next.js API Authentication, routing, metadata, report requests and integration REST/API layer AI service Python + FastAPI OCR orchestration, extraction, NLP, RAG, validation and analytics AI processing service Document processing Python libraries + OCR PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, image and scanned document processing Normalized records AI/NLP Embeddings + LLM + NLP libraries Retrieval, summarization, Q&A;, topic identification Grounded answers/topics Database PostgreSQL / MongoDB Metadata, extracted records, validation results and audit records Structured store File storage Object storage / controlled filesystem Original files and processed artifacts Document repository Vector search pgvector / FAISS / vector DB Semantic retrieval for grounded Q&A; Relevant source chunks Reporting Python + DOCX/PDF generation Generate structured reports and export artifacts Draft reports 6. End-to-End Processing Pipeline 1 User uploads an authorized document or data package. 2 System creates a document ID, checksum/hash, source metadata and processing record. 3 File type is detected and routed to the appropriate parser. 4 Scanned pages are passed through OCR; native digital documents use direct text/table extraction. 5 Extracted content is normalized into text blocks, tables, figures, metadata and page-level references. 6 A document classifier identifies the broad document type, such as production report, geological report, mine report, administrative correspondence or statistical statement. 7 Important fields and numerical values are extracted into structured records.

SIH Problem Statement 26023 | Prototype & Real-Data Testing Document 8 Validation rules check formats, ranges, totals, dates, units and cross-document consistency. 9 Text is chunked and indexed for keyword and semantic retrieval. 10 Topic identification and word-cloud analysis are generated for selected document collections. 11 The report engine uses structured data and approved templates to generate a draft report. 12 The query engine retrieves relevant source evidence before generating an answer. 13 The user reviews the result, corrections are captured, and the final approved artifact is exported. 7. Core Functional Modules A. Document Ingestion & Digitization • Multi-format upload: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV, PNG/JPG. • OCR for scanned documents. • Document metadata and checksum generation. • Duplicate detection and version tracking. B. AI Extraction & Structuring • Named field extraction for mine/project/report/date/area/production-related fields. • Table extraction and normalization. • Unit normalization where a known unit conversion is defined. • Confidence score for extracted fields. C. Validation & Traceability • Rule-based validation for totals and consistency. • Cross-document comparison. • Exception flags for missing or contradictory values. • Source citation: document, page, table/cell or text span where available. D. Automated Report Generation • Select a reporting period and data scope. • Populate a standard report template. • Insert validated tables and summaries. • Attach source references and validation status. • Export to DOCX/PDF. E. Word Cloud & Topic Identification • Clean stop words and common boilerplate. • Generate frequency-based word cloud. • Extract representative topics. • Show representative source documents/chunks for each topic. F. AI Query & Response • Natural-language questions over authorized documents. • Hybrid keyword + semantic retrieval. • Answer generation constrained to retrieved evidence.

SIH Problem Statement 26023 | Prototype & Real-Data Testing Document • Show source references supporting the answer. • Return 'insufficient evidence' when the repository does not support a reliable answer. 8. Real-Data Prototype Testing Strategy The prototype should be tested with real operational data only when the team has explicit authorization to access and process it. If direct operational data cannot be used in the hackathon environment, create a sanitized test set that preserves the structure, document complexity, tables, terminology and typical errors of real records. 8.1 Recommended Test Dataset Data Category Example Test Material What to Test Ground Truth Scanned PDF Scanned monthly/annual report pages OCR + field extraction Manually verified values Native PDF Digital technical/report document Text/table extraction Verified text/table records Excel Production/statistical spreadsheet Cell mapping + calculations Known spreadsheet values Word Administrative/technical report Text + metadata extraction Verified fields Images Photographed/scanned table or chart OCR + visual extraction Manually transcribed reference Historical archive Older reports with different formats Robustness across formats Sampled verified records Mixed collection Multiple years/documents Cross-document search and Q&A; Question-answer benchmark 8.2 Ground-Truth Process 1 Select a representative sample of documents. 2 Manually verify the target fields and important numerical values. 3 Store the verified values separately as the benchmark ground truth. 4 Run the prototype without manually correcting its output. 5 Compare extracted values with ground truth. 6 Record exact, incorrect, missing and hallucinated values. 7 Calculate accuracy and other metrics. 8 Investigate failures by document type, scan quality, table complexity and field type. 9 Repeat after model/prompt/rule improvements. 9. Evaluation Metrics Metric Measurement Purpose Field Extraction Accuracy Correct extracted target fields / total target fields × 100 Measures structured extraction quality. OCR Accuracy Character/word-level comparison on sampled ground truth Measures scan-to-text quality. Numerical Accuracy Correct numerical values / verified numerical values × 100 Critical for production/statistical figures. Validation Detection Rate Correctly detected issues / known issues × 100 Measures consistency-check performance. Report Automation Rate Automated reporting steps / total repetitive reporting steps × 100 Quantifies reduction in repetitive work. Report Preparation Time Compare baseline manual time vs prototype time Measures time savings. Q&A; Groundedness Supported answers / evaluated answers × 100 Measures whether answers are supported by source evidence. Q&A; Retrieval Recall Relevant source items retrieved / relevant source items available Measures retrieval quality. Topic Quality Human review of representative topics and source evidence Evaluates topic identification usefulness. Important: The final accuracy/automation percentages should be calculated from the team's actual benchmark results. Do not present target values as achieved results.

Real-Data Security and Governance • Use only data for which the team has explicit authorization. • Separate production/authorized data from development sample data. • Do not hard-code credentials, API keys or passwords. • Encrypt data in transit and at rest where applicable. • Implement role-based access for users and administrators. • Maintain an audit trail for uploads, processing, corrections, report generation and approvals. • Keep original files immutable; store corrected/processed versions separately. • Use checksums/hashes to identify document versions and detect accidental modification. • Mask or remove sensitive information from datasets used for demonstrations when authorization is not available. • Define retention and deletion rules appropriate to the organization's requirements. • Prevent the AI model from treating unsupported generated content as official facts. • Require human review before an AI-generated report becomes an official report. 12.
